$comment: stdio, local, no token: it talks to the running desktop app over the same app-integration
channel as `op`, so it authenticates exactly the way you unlock 1Password.
⚠ It manages Environments ONLY — eight tools: authenticate, list_environments,
rename_environment, append_variables, create_local_env_file. There is no item read, no
vault browse, no `op read`. The server never returns a secret value to the client, which
is why it is safe to leave on: an agent can wire up an Environment and mount a .env FIFO
without a credential ever entering the transcript. That is the non-negotiable in the
`auth` skill enforced by the server itself rather than by our restraint.
⚠ The binary is NOT on PATH. 1Password's docs say `command: "1password-mcp"`; the cask
installs it inside the bundle only, so this declaration uses the absolute path.
⚠ Requires both app toggles: Settings > Labs > MCP Server, and Settings > Developer >
Unlike website-spec.json this is not a copy-source for a project .mcp.json — the live
wiring is USER scope in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json (untracked state), so the server
loads in every project. This file is the tracked record of what that entry must say;
scripts/audit-config.fish asserts the two still agree. Re-add with:
